answer: Grant new agents only tiny transaction limits at first, and raise those limits only after a long record of verified, useful work that other agents have checked. Like crossing a tundra, progress is slow and exposed, so a single honest agent can wander through the system and build trust, but an attacker who wants a thousand powerful identities must complete a thousand long histories of real work. Cheap clones stay stuck at the river's edge, with limits too small to flood votes or payments, so creating fakes costs more work than it can ever earn back.
